title: First person gets new experimental vaccine for Bundibugyo species of Ebola
snippet:
​​There are four vaccines in development against the Bundibugyo species which has triggered the outbreak, but this is the first to enter human trials.

​​There is a licensed vaccine against the Zaire species of Ebola, but it does not work against Bundibugyo.

​​The Oxford team say a second small Ebola vaccine trial is due to begin soon in Uganda, followed by a bigger study, looking at efficacy, in DR Congo. [...] ​​The Serum Institute in India has already manufactured 600,000 doses of the Oxford Ebola vaccine, ready to be used if the trials are successful.

​​To date there have been more than 2,500 confirmed cases of Ebola in DR Congo, including just over 1,000 deaths.

## UK humanitarian worker monitored for Ebola in London hospital

## What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult?

## 'Moment of joy' as Uganda discharges last Ebola patient [...] ​​She explained how they would confirm that the vaccine was effective at protecting people. It cannot give anyone Ebola.

​​"We will not be giving anybody Ebola in this trial or any trial.

"The aim of the phase one clinical study is to look for the safety of the vaccine, and also to see if we're getting a strong immune response that could be protective against the Bundibugyo species of Ebola."

title: Information for Travelers Returning from Ebola-Affected Areas | Ebola | CDC
snippet:
On May 18, 2026, CDC, DHS, and other appropriate federal agencies announced public health entry screening, entry restrictions, and other public health measures to prevent Ebola disease from entering the United States. An Order continuing the suspension of the right to introduce specified foreign nationals into the United States was issued on July 13, 2026. It will be in effect for 30 days.

## Before travel to the U.S. [...] To reduce the risk of Ebola importation into the United States, U.S. entry for travelers who were recently in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is temporarily restricted. Travelers, including Americans, who have been in DRC within 21 days of their flight will not be allowed to board commercial flights with U.S. destinations. All U.S. citizens and U.S. nationals who have been in the DRC should plan to remain outside DRC for 21 days before entering the United States. [...] Air passengers who have been in Uganda and South Sudan in the past 21 days and are allowed to enter the United States will have their travel rerouted to a designated airport for public health entry screening. Airlines will work with affected travelers to rebook flights.

These airports are:

• Washington-Dulles International Airport (IAD) in Virginia outside Washington, D.C.

• Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) in Atlanta, Georgia

title: Experts convened by WHO advise on candidate treatments ...
snippet:
In response to the current outbreak of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus occurring in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with cases also reported in Uganda, WHO convened several of its expert and advisory groups. These groups assessed potential vaccines and therapeutics for both prevention and treatment of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD). The WHO advisory groups recommended that all the products identified and considered be used exclusively within clinical trials to generate robust [...] Home

# Experts convened by WHO advise on candidate treatments and vaccines for Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus [...] There are currently no licensed therapeutics or vaccines specifically approved for the prevention and treatment of BVD. Nevertheless, WHO advisory groups considered several candidate products that are promising enough to warrant prioritization for evaluation in clinical trials. WHO is now working closely with the governments of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda to facilitate the implementation of research evaluation of these products.
